title: Interleukin-1 Inhibition to Improve the Response of Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Resistant to Cytoreductive Treatment
official: Interleukin-1 Inhibition to Improve the Response of Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Resistant to Cytoreductive Treatment
summary:
Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) - polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and primary myelofibrosis - are characterized by excessive myeloid proliferation driven by mutations affecting the JAK2, CALR, and MPL genes, resulting in constitutive activation of hematopoietic cytokine signaling pathways. These hematological malignancies carry an increased risk of thrombosis and may evolve toward secondary myelofibrosis or acute leukemia. Bone marrow inflammation, particularly through interleukin-1 (IL-1), plays a major role in clonal expansion and the clinical expression of these diseases, as demonstrated by preclinical models showing the beneficial effect of its inhibition.

Anakinra, an IL-1 receptor antagonist widely used in rheumatology but never evaluated in MPNs, represents a promising therapeutic option. This proof-of-concept study will randomize 50 patients with a suboptimal response to cytoreductive therapy into two arms: anakinra 100 mg/day administered subcutaneously in combination with ongoing cytoreductive therapy (n=25), or cytoreductive therapy alone (n=25). The primary endpoint will be the reduction in serum calprotectin levels, a key inflammatory marker of the IL-1 loop that has recently demonstrated prognostic relevance in MPNs. Secondary endpoints will include improvements in hematological parameters, driver mutation allelic burden, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and quality of life.

This study represents an essential step toward larger trials aimed at demonstrating a durable reduction in thrombotic risk and disease progression.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of MPN: PV, ET, or PMF according to WHO criteria
* Stable cytoreductive therapy for at least 6 months
* Incomplete hematologic response according to ELN criteria, excluding bone marrow, OR complete hematologic response with anemia in ET, OR persistence of general clinical symptoms (fever, night sweats, pruritus, fatigue \> 5/10 on VAS)
* Adult patient capable of providing informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Recurrent or poorly controlled infections
* Thrombocytopenia \< 100 G/L
* Neutropenia \< 1 G/L
* Hypersensitivity to the active substance, any excipients, or proteins derived from Escherichia coli
* Concomitant immunosuppressive therapy
* Refusal to participate
* Patient under legal protection (guardianship, curatorship, etc.)
* Patients unable to consent.
* Positive urine pregnancy test at screening / pregnant or breastfeeding women.
* Lack of understanding of questionnaires or inability to follow up.
* Women of childbearing potential unwilling to use a highly effective contraceptive methods
